speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with a limp and localized pain, but no fever or acute distress. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me which part of your body hurts and how long ago the limp started?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the left knee pain and limping without trauma or fever are concerning. Given his age, I need to clarify if he also reports pain in his left hip, thigh, or buttock when you touch or move those areas? Additionally, does the pain wake him up at night or make him refuse to bear weight entirely?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Understood, the pain is strictly localized to the left knee without night pain or refusal to bear weight. To determine if this is a referred hip pathology or a direct knee issue, can you tell me if your child can fully bend and straighten the left knee, and does pressing on the knee joint itself cause pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of isolated knee pain with a limp in a 7-year-old male is highly suspicious for slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE), even though the pain is referred. To confirm this, I need to assess hip range of motion. Does your child have difficulty rotating his left leg inward or outward, or does it feel stiff when I try to move the hip?

REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_XRay_AP

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The denial of systemic symptoms like weight loss or rash helps rule out infection or malignancy. Now, based on the X-ray images I have requested, do you see any widening of the left hip joint or a slipped appearance of the femoral head? This will confirm if it is indeed Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE).
